name: input.keyboard.key_up
description: Release a virtual key if held by anything (this connection or another). Idempotent — returns `OK 0` whether or not the key was held. Use to lift a key held by `input.keyboard.key_down`, or as a cross-connection fail-safe to recover from a stuck state. Same user32-layer-only delivery as `input.keyboard.key` — DirectInput / RawInput targets won't observe the release event. See `spec/operators/05-footguns.md` for the capability boundary. Per issue #70.

x-output-schema.description: Empty body — wire response is the literal `OK 0`. Idempotent: no error if the key wasn't held. The agent removes the vk from any connection's held-input set (cross-connection cleanup permitted; see lifecycle §2.8).

x-implementations.name: send_input
x-implementations.description: Win32 `SendInput` with INPUT_KEYBOARD + `KEYEVENTF_KEYUP`. Always issued — the OS no-ops gracefully when the key wasn't actually down.

x-implementations.name: keybd_event
x-implementations.description: Win32 `keybd_event` legacy fallback for NT 4 / 9x where SendInput is unavailable.

windows-modern.description: SendInput with KEYEVENTF_KEYUP. Agent removes the vk from the per-connection held-input set (and any other connection's set that holds it — cross-connection release is the documented fail-safe). Idempotent — no `not_held` error since the verb's purpose is cleanup.

windows-classic.description: SendInput on NT 5+; keybd_event on NT 4 / 9x. Same idempotent cross-connection-release semantics as modern.
